report.clinical_summary: Patient presents with a 2-week neck lump (pea-sized, slightly tender, fixed) and 1-month fatigue affecting work, hobbies, and social life. On blood pressure medication for 1+ year (well controlled) and occasional OTC analgesics. Anxious about CLL (blood cancer) and its potential impact on work, finances, and emotional wellbeing. Limited understanding of CLL and treatment options. Coping through social support (wife, friends) and lifestyle self-care.

evidence.quote: Even simple tasks at work take more effort than usual, and by the end of the day, I'm completely drained.
It also impacts my hobbies and personal life.
When we go out for dinner with friends or spend time with family, it's harder to engage in conversations or activities that I used to enjoy without feeling exhausted.
If my condition progressed and I couldn't work anymore, my biggest worry would be how this might affect our family finances
worried about the emotional impact on myself and my wife, as well as how it might change our lives overall

consequences.reasoning: Patient describes substantial impact on work (simple tasks take more effort, completely drained), hobbies, personal life, and social activities. Worries about losing work entirely and the financial/emotional impact. This is significant impact on daily functioning and roles.

evidence.quote: I've only really started getting concerned in the past few weeks since my wife pointed out the lump in my neck.
Before then, I was just feeling more tired than usual and putting it down to stress at work or maybe just getting older.
So while I'm not entirely sure how quickly things might progress, I would have thought that something like this would be caught early on if it were going to develop slowly over time.

As for how long this process might take, I don't know for sure, but I understand that these things can sometimes take a while depending on the results and what needs to be done next. So, if it takes several weeks or even months, I'm prepared for that — as long as we're making progress and getting closer to understanding what's going on.

Doesn't have clear sense of illness duration but is prepared for longer process. Somewhere between uncertainty and acceptance of longer timeline.
